**Japan Operations significantly outperforms US and EU across operational metrics, while all regions show concerning supply chain inefficiencies.**

| Metric | US (1000) | Japan (5000) | EU (2100) | Source App |
|--------|-----------|--------------|-----------|------------|
| Net Margin | 25.3% | 24.0% | 22.9% | FIN |

**Working capital efficiency varies**: Japan maintains the lowest cash conversion cycle at 66 days vs US 54.9 days, though negative net working capital across all entities suggests strong supplier payment terms (WCP).

**Supply chain costs**: Late delivery costs range from $362K (Japan) to $3.6M (US), representing 2.4% vs 24.2% of net income respectively (SCM vs FIN comparison using demo crosswalk).

## Recommended Actions

1. **Replicate Japan's operational model** in US and EU plants - investigate their maintenance, scheduling, and quality processes
2. **Implement enterprise-wide contract management** - 70% off-contract spend represents significant cost leakage and compliance risk
3. **Address US supply chain urgency** - $3.6M late costs suggest systemic delivery failures requiring immediate intervention
4. **Standardize cross-regional best practices** using the shared enterprise ontology to ensure consistent KPI measurement and improvement tracking

4. **Governance**: Establish master data stewardship for the golden entity creation process before expanding beyond demo scope
